key_insight: This work delivers a very large video reasoning suite that enables systematic study of spatiotemporal reasoning (continuity, interaction, causality) at scale, revealing how video reasoning capabilities emerge and scale with data and compute.
problem_solved: The absence of large-scale training data, standardized tasks, and benchmarks has prevented rigorous study of video reasoning and its scaling behavior.
method: Assemble a large, diverse video dataset annotated for spatiotemporal reasoning phenomena (continuity, interaction, causality).
Design a suite of standardized tasks and evaluation protocols that probe temporal structure and multi-object interactions.
Benchmark models and run scaling experiments to quantify performance trends as data/compute/architecture scale.
impact: Provides practitioners with a standard dataset and evaluation framework to build, compare, and scale video-reasoning models, informing dataset collection and model design decisions. Accelerates progress toward models that reason about dynamic visual scenes rather than only generating high-quality frames.
visual_elements: Dataset composition infographic (sources, size, task breakdown) — pie chart or stacked bars
Annotated video timeline showing examples of continuity, interaction, and causal events
Task matrix mapping tasks to reasoning skills and expected difficulty
Scaling curves showing model performance vs dataset size / compute
paper_title: A Very Big Video Reasoning Suite
paper_authors: Maijunxian Wang, Ruisi Wang, Juyi Lin, Ran Ji, Thaddäus Wiedemer
